bib.title: BitFit: Simple Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning for Transformer-based Masked Language-models

question: Can fine-tuning only the bias terms of a pre-trained masked LM match full fine-tuning?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning is mainly about exposing knowledge induced by language-modeling training rather than learning new task-specific knowledge, so few parameters should suffice.
contributions: BitFit: train only bias terms and the task classifier
Competitive with full FT on small-to-medium data, with Diff-Pruning and Adapters on GLUE
Only query and intermediate-MLP biases (0.04%) retain most performance

method.summary: Freeze all weight matrices and layer-norm gains of BERT/RoBERTa; train only bias vectors plus a linear classifier on [CLS]. Evaluated on GLUE, PTB POS and SQuAD v1.0.

datasets.name: GLUE (8 tasks, no WNLI)
datasets.size: QNLI 105k, SST-2 67k, MNLI 393k, CoLA 8.5k, MRPC 3.7k, STS-B 7k, RTE 2.5k, QQP 364k train

training.objective: task loss with linear head on [CLS]
training.lr: bias-only: search {1e-4, 4e-4, 7e-4, 1e-3}; full FT: {1e-5, 2e-5, 3e-5, 5e-5}; RoBERTa: 1e-4 bias-only, 1e-5 full FT
training.epochs: bias-only converged in 8 or fewer epochs for most tasks, up to 20 on others
training.seeds: 5 models with 5 random seeds, mean and std reported

other.best_lr_table: Table 6 lists per-task best LR for BERT-Base and BERT-Large

metrics.name: GLUE per-task
metrics.definition: QNLI/SST-2/RTE acc; MNLI matched/mismatched acc; CoLA Matthews corr; MRPC and QQP F1; STS-B Spearman

metrics.name: SQuAD EM and F1
metrics.definition: exact match and F1 on validation

eval.protocol: mean of 5 seeds; dev and test (Table 1); Diff-Pruning/Adapters numbers copied from original papers

evidence.quote: we used initial learning rates in {1e-5, 2e-5, 3e-5, 5e-5}, and for the bias-only experiments we used initial learning rates in {1e-4, 4e-4, 7e-4, 1e-

results.claim: BitFit on BERT-Large reaches the GLUE dev average of full fine-tuning (84.2 vs 84.1) with 0.08% of parameters
results.setup: BERT-Large, GLUE dev, 9 tasks, mean of 5 seeds

results.claim: Bias terms make up 0.09% (BERT-Base) and 0.08% (BERT-Large) of parameters
results.quote: in BERTBASE and BERTLARGE bias parameters make up 0.09% and 0.08% of the total number of parameters in each model, respectively

results.claim: Tuning only query and intermediate-MLP biases uses 0.04% of parameters and scores 81.1 vs 82.4 for all biases
results.table: Table 3, row bm2, bq, column Avg.

results.claim: Random subset of the same size (0.09%) is much worse than bias terms: 78.5 uniform, 79.5 row/col vs 82.4
results.table: Table 3, row rand uniform, column Avg.

results.claim: A fully frozen BERT-Base scores 62.1 average
results.setup: BERT-Base, only classifier trained, GLUE dev

results.claim: BitFit trails full fine-tuning on the largest task QQP (85.4 vs 87.5 F1)
On GLUE test BERT-Large BitFit averages 80.9 vs 81.8 (Full-FT, Guo et al.) and 81.1 Adapters
results.setup: BERT-Large, GLUE test; baselines copied from Guo 2020 and Houlsby 2019
results.note: Adapters row 3.6% params, Full-FT test numbers are reported from other papers; QNLI not directly comparable (test set updated).

results.claim: BERT-Base BitFit matches full FT on average (82.4 vs 82.3); RoBERTa-Base 84.6 vs 85.3
results.table: Table 2, row BB BitFit, column Avg.

results.claim: PTB POS-tagging: BitFit 97.2, 97.4, 97.1 vs Full-FT 97.2, 97.4, 97.2 for BERT-Base, BERT-Large, RoBERTa-Base
results.quote: Full-FT results for BERTBASE, BERTLARGE and RoBERTaBASE are 97.2, 97.4, 97.2, while BitFit results are 97.2, 97.4, 97.1.

results.claim: BitFit beats Full-FT on SQuAD v1.0 with small training subsets, trend reverses with more data
results.setup: BERT-Base, SQuAD v1.0 validation, increasing subsets; values only in Fig 2/6 (not in text)

results.claim: BitFit has about 6x fewer trainable parameters than Diff-Pruning and 45x fewer than Adapters

limits: Only BERT-family masked LMs; no decoder/large LLMs
BitFit loses to full FT on large datasets (QQP, MNLI, and SQuAD with more data)
Diff-Pruning and Adapter baselines copied from other papers
Hardware, schedule, warmup, sequence length not stated
QNLI test not comparable to earlier numbers
Why bias terms work is left open
